(Currently Amended) A method of impeding Leishmaniasis transmission in [[humans or animals]] __dogs__ comprising administering to [[an animal or human]] __a dog__ a composition comprising Leishmania [[promastigotes or Leishmania amastigotes]] __donovani promastigote__ fractions called "Fucose Mannose Ligand" (FML) and saponin.

7. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 4 wherein the Leishmania [[promastigotes or Leishmania amastigotes]] __donovani promastigote__ fractions called "Fucose Mannose Ligand" (FML) comprise a glycoprotein complex containing 29% of neutral sugar, 44% of protein, 11% of phosphate and hexoamines traces composed by protein bands with molecular weight ranging from 9 to 95 kDa, some protein bands having carbohydrates: 36 and 54 to 68 kDa, the FML glycidic portion presenting 10% of fucose and 47% of mannose, 30% of glucose, 12% of galactose and xylose traces, aminoacids containing 10 to 20% of glutamic acid, alanine, aspartic acid and glycine, 5 to 10% of serine, histidine, lysine, leucine, threonine, proline and valine, and 2 to 5% of arginine, methionine, isoleucine, tyrosine and phenylalanine.
